A1.justification: Both complete 45-page PDFs describe the same ANOVA-TPNN research, including Appendices A–N. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that differences are confined to the version/date stamp and Appendix A.4.

before.justification: v4 reports original component-selection, prediction, stability, and runtime experiments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and the appendices, including synthetic, tabular, and image-data evaluations.

M1.justification: ANOVA-TPNN, NBM-TPNN, their training procedures, and monotone constraints are unchanged. The revised coefficient definition belongs to the approximation proof, not the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same three synthetic functions, nine standard tabular datasets, three high-dimensional datasets, and CelebA, with unchanged tasks and test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including NAM, NBM, NODE-GAM, XGB, DNN, Spline-GAM, Decision Tree, and Kernel-SHAP in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: The 70/10/20 splits, preprocessing, evaluation metrics, hyperparameter searches, model configurations, and training settings are identical.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same basis-count, initialization, stability, monotonicity, SHAP, ReLU, sum-to-zero, post-processing, and spline-outlier analyses.

E5.justification: Repeated-run information and uncertainty reporting are identical, including ten-split prediction evaluations, five-dataset stability visualizations, and reported means and standard deviations.

E6.justification: Tables 1–27 and Figures 1–22 contain identical results. Numerical values, rankings, runtime measurements, and qualitative experimental findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Below Eq. (10), Appendix A.4 replaces expectations over X_S with integrals under explicitly defined P_S, the product of population marginal distributions P_j. This specifies the proof's averaging measure, a distinction relevant for dependent features. The theorem statements, approximation rates, and remaining proof are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about identifiable and stable component estimation, universal approximation, competitive prediction, and the NBM-TPNN extension.

C2.justification: Interpretations of stability, outlier robustness, monotonicity, and post-processing are unchanged, as is the limitation concerning high-order interactions in high-dimensional data.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, processing instructions, and code-access information are unchanged, including Appendix B and the source-code link.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to prior functional ANOVA and neural additive models are identical.

P1.justification: Appendix A.4 adds a short explanation defining the product measure, and the arXiv version/date stamp changes. Section organization and the remaining prose are unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised integral display and explanatory sentence produce localized spacing and line-break changes on page 19. All figures, tables, captions, and other substantive page layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 explicitly identifies the product-marginal measure used for the higher-order approximation coefficients in Appendix A.4, reducing ambiguity in the proof construction. This provides a limited improvement in theoretical clarity; the theorem statements, empirical evidence, and principal conclusions remain unchanged.
